newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends quiet session higher on weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends quiet session higher on weather.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures ended a dull session slightly higher on Friday amid perceptions weather patterns are not conducive to crop development and harvest, traders said.
"There are some people who are concerned a little bit about the dryness in the western Corn Belt," said Warren King, wheat analyst for Cargill Investor Services.
"You've got some moisture in the Plains that could slow harvest a little bit and it's still cool and wet in the east but there's really nothing in here today we didn't know this morning."
Heavy rains moved across central Texas on Friday morning, further delaying the hard red winter wheat harvest, cash grain merchandisers said.
Showers were also in the forecast for the eastern Corn Belt. Traders said wet weather in the eastern U.S. Midwest could increase scab and disease problems.
Some sources also pointed to dry conditions in Australia. Drought in the Australian state of New South Wales covered 45 percent of the state, up five percent from last month.
Wheat ended 4-1/2 to two cents per bushel higher with July up 3-1/2 at $3.59-1/2.
On the day, Cargill Inc was a noted buyer of two million bushels December and LIT bought 3.5 million July, pit sources said. FCC and Term Commodities each sold one million September.
In options trade, FCC bought 225 July $3.60 calls at eight cents and Refco Inc sold 200 September $3.80 puts at 26-1/2 cents.
Volume was estimated by CBOT at 13,000 contracts, below the 14,256 traded on Thursday.
